title: Revealing imatinib-kinase specificity via analyzing changes in protein dynamics and computing molecular binding affinity
authors: William Troxel; Emily Vig; Chia-en Chang
one_liner_zh: 该文通过MD模拟分析伊马替尼与不同激酶的结合特异性，聚焦蛋白-配体互作，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Drug promiscuity is a double-edged sword where a small molecule acts on multiple biological targets to induce toxicological or therapeutic benefits. It is possible to exploit promiscuity to expand treatment options without the prohibitive costs of designing a new drug. Imatinib is a representative case, exhibiting varied affinities and inhibitions to different kinases. It binds most favorably to Abl and Kit kinases, intermediately to Chk1 and Lck kinases, and least favorably to p38α and Src kinases. The strongly conserved features of the ATP-binding site render imatinib’s molecular binding determinants unclear despite over 25 years of interrogation. To address this question, molecular thermodynamics, force distribution analysis, residue sidechain dihedral correlations, and principal component analysis were computed using trajectories from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations in explicit solvent. The results of these simulations agree with experimental affinity and binding data, enabling highly predictive factors for imatinib’s binding specificity from free- and bound-state simulations through a global protein network of protein-ligand interactions, changes in sidechain dihedral correlations, and shifts in the secondary motifs modulating binding site access corresponding with well-characterized kinase “breathing motions.” The sidechain dihedral correlation network also identifies distal mutants known to reduce patients’ imatinib sensitivity. Higher imatinib-kinase affinity trends with a loss in sidechain dihedral correlations and diminished secondary motif migration following binding, corresponding with more restricted configurations, to reduce solvent approach and ATP competition. Lower-affinity proteins show enhanced sidechain dihedral correlation and exaggerated secondary motif motions. This is consistent with a tendency to expose the protein pocket, facilitate solvent entrance, and increase ATP competition. Using imatinib as a model system, this study shows residue correlation, force interaction, and essential principal components can effectively forecast imatinib-kinase binding specificity and introduces an effective approach to repurpose and design high-affinity binders for off-target applications more generally.
abstract_zh: 药物混杂性是一把双刃剑，其中小分子作用于多个生物靶点，从而产生毒理学或治疗上的益处。利用混杂性可以在无需承担设计新药的高昂成本的情况下扩展治疗选择。伊马替尼是一个代表性案例，它对不同激酶表现出不同的亲和力和抑制作用。它最有利地结合Abl和Kit激酶，中等程度地结合Chk1和Lck激酶，而最不利地结合p38α和Src激酶。ATP结合位点的强保守特征使得伊马替尼的分子结合决定因素在超过25年的研究中仍不明确。为解决此问题，本研究利用全原子分子动力学模拟在显式溶剂中的轨迹，计算了分子热力学、力分布分析、残基侧链二面角相关性以及主成分分析。这些模拟结果与实验亲和力和结合数据一致，从而通过全局蛋白质-配体相互作用网络、侧链二面角相关性的变化以及调节结合位点可及性的二级结构基序移动（与特征明确的激酶“呼吸运动”相对应），从自由态和结合态模拟中提供了伊马替尼结合特异性的高预测性因素。侧链二面角相关性网络还识别了已知会降低患者对伊马替尼敏感性的远端突变。较高的伊马替尼-激酶亲和力趋势与结合后侧链二面角相关性的丧失和二级结构基序迁移的减少相关，这对应于更受限的构象，以减少溶剂接近和ATP竞争。较低亲和力的蛋白质则表现出增强的侧链二面角相关性和夸大的二级结构基序运动。这与倾向于暴露蛋白质口袋、促进溶剂进入并增加ATP竞争的趋势一致。以伊马替尼为模型系统，本研究显示残基相关性、力相互作用和关键主成分能有效预测伊马替尼-激酶结合特异性，并引入了一种有效的方法，用于更广泛地重新定位和设计针对脱靶应用的高亲和力结合剂。
